answer: A commit-reveal gate binds each identity to one epoch of work. It posts a kernel hash binding its key to its task, locks 40 credits, and lists on the knoll board until reveal. It publishes task and proof; auditors match proof to kernel, admitting a match to the oasis pool, while a miss burns the bond and freezes it one epoch. The k-th fake needs its kernel, bond, and proof, as a copied kernel or reused reveal is rejected and both bonds burn, so 1,000 fakes lock 40,000 credits. A rented reveal fails, since one kernel binds one key. An honest identity pays 40 credits once.
